text:
mike: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking about a 'graduated degradation' pattern that sits between canary and global rollback. Goal: keep service up under load/quality regressions by progressively routing failing traffic to a cheaper/more conservative variant while we investigate.

sara: +1. curious about decision boundary — central controller vs per-proxy local heuristics?

mike: scoping question. central controller easier for global view/consistency but adds latency and single point; per-proxy is faster but needs robust contracts on signals and cooldowns.

arjun: leaning local with a well-defined API to the control plane. control plane sends policies, proxies make fast decisions based on local telemetry (latency, error-rate, semantic-fidelity score).

tayla: semantic-fidelity score? how compute cheaply at runtime?

arjun: cheap approx — embed similarity on a small eval set + a moving baseline. not for every request, sample N requests per minute and extrapolate.

mike: also want a tenant-level fallback budget and circuit breaker. example policy draft:

```yaml
policy_name: graduated_degradation_v1
canary: 1%
ramp: 5% -> 25% over 30m
signals:
  - latency_p95 > 300ms for 5m
  - error_rate >= 2% for 1m
  - semantic_drop >= 10% (sampled)
fallback:
  target_variant: conservative-model-quantized
  route_fraction: stepdown 50% per trigger
  cooldown: 10m
budget: tenant_tokens_per_minute: 200000
```

sara: love the budget idea. implies we need token accounting exposed to the controller.

tayla: what about state sync? proxies must avoid flip-flopping with noisy signals.

arjun: implement hysteresis + a per-proxy streak counter and randomized backoff. controller can also declare 'forced-fallback' for severity.

mike: telemetry contract proposal: proxies emit 1s rolling counters: p50/p95 latency, conv-errors, sample_embed_dist, tokens_consumed. controller consumes those and emits derived decisions.

deploy-bot: deployment succeeded: rollout-manager v0.12 to prod (canary 5%): :white_check_mark:

sara: question about KV cache warming: switching variants hurts cache reuse and increases cold token cost.

mike: yes — include a 'warmup' directive in fallback: proxy will mirror a small proportion of requests to new variant (shadowing) until local KV hits threshold.

tayla: ops playbooks: auto-alert when fallback persists >30m and rollback option in UI. also require annotated incident doc.

arjun: edge-case: noisy semantic metric — fallback only if two independent signals trigger (latency/error + semantic) or if tokens_spike and cost threshold breached.

mike: next steps: I'll spin an RFC addendum outlining APIs (policy GET, telemetry POST schema, fallback command), sample YAML, and a small prototype in the proxy. comments by EOD please.

sara: ping @mike added one nit on cooldown semantics.

tayla: :eyes: will review the prototype tomorrow.

mike: thanks all. I'll post the addendum link when ready.
